chunks: What Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: Whoever is performing tamattu' and cannot find a sacrificial offering, then he must fast three days during the hajj and seven when he returns to his family. If he misses that, and he remains after the departure, he should fast three days in Makkah; and if he does not remain, he should fast on the road or among his family. And if he remains in Makkah and wishes to fast the seven, he should leave off fasting for the length of his travel to his family, or for a month, then fast after that.

key_terms.ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ: the three days of fasting required during hajj
key_terms.هَدْيًا: a sacrificial offering required in the pilgrimage context
key_terms.ٱلسَّبْعَةَ: the seven additional days of fasting after return
key_terms.ٱلصَّدَرِ: the departure from Mina after the rites
key_terms.ٱلطَّرِيقِ: the route of travel on which fasting may be performed
key_terms.ٱلْحَجِّ: the pilgrimage period in which part of the fasting is observed

ai.seo_question: What should a person performing tamattu' hajj do if he cannot find a sacrificial offering?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for one performing hajj al-tamattu' who cannot obtain the sacrificial offering. It outlines when the required three days and seven days of fasting are to be observed, including cases of remaining in Makkah, traveling, or returning home.
